data.name: Goetia
data.detailed_description:
The ruins of any village are the silent testament to its final moments. The ruins of Oakmarsh are no different. Their telling silence, the dust blanketing what was once a quiet village near Coventry.

The name of a manor and the family that lived within. A perverted and mad lineage, a clan whose final members devoted their life to mysticism and fanatical experiments. I am Abigail. Abigail Blackwood. Recently risen from the grave, I know nothing about the last 40 years of my family’s history... But obviously somebody is keen on seeing me lift the veil on what happened in Oakmarsh - to what led to the downfall of Blackwood Manor. And it seems like I have no choice in the matter…

Key Features
  • A 2D world of Victorian mystery.
  • Over 90 rooms to explore.
  • Five vast and diverse areas to discover - Blackwood Manor is surrounded by ruins, woods, caves and an abandoned village.
  • A progressive-rock and ambient-inspired soundtrack.
  • Use your ability to walk through walls in order to reach secret rooms and areas.
  • Possess objects like a poltergeist to lift them, use them, combine them, make them float in the air, pile them up… well, you’re a ghost after all, behave like one!
  • Solve puzzles in more than one way by discovering hidden rooms and special features, such as new ghostly powers.
  • Delve into Blackwood’s story: 40 years have passed, and many things have changed since Abigail’s death.
  • Feel free to explore! You can travel through the world of Goetia however you like - and if you get stuck, simply backtrack and explore another area.

reviews.review:
To start things off, I will point out the positive aspects of the game, since there are a couple of them! The premise of the game is very interesting, and the atmosphere is spooky and intriguing. These things are effective at drawing you in and making you motivated to discover the secrets of your family's past.

Despite this, the process of actually completing this game made me hate it with such intensity that it will go down in history as one of the most frustrating and unenjoyable games I have ever endured.

The puzzles are so ridiculously obscure that even the guide outlining the full completion walkthrough states that they do not understand how anyone is meant to figure out the answers to some of the puzzles. Obviously it can be satisfying to solve a challenging riddle sometimes, but that does not apply here because knowing the solutions still doesn't make the puzzles make sense. It's not even a skill issue either; some of the puzzles are beyond ridiculous. One puzzle had a series of very vague hints in the form of prose that apparently were meant to send you on a quest to four (?) different areas of the house to notice one VERY SUBTLE shape in each room that you are somehow meant to know is significant. Then you are meant to find slips of paper for the shapes and arrange them in one specific way for no apparent reason. And over the course of this puzzle, from the riddles to the arrangement of the little paper scraps, the game gives zero indication whatsoever that you are making any progress or even doing the correct thing at all. You are expected to just notice all of these things independently and put it all together at the end with zero guidance. It's simply astounding.

From an accessibility standpoint, the game struggles significantly in a few major ways. Most of the gameplay involves reading notes, books, posters, text boxes, etc., and most of this text is VERY SMALL with no way to increase the font size. I spent so much time squinting that I'm surprised I didn't get a headache. Also, the map is TERRIBLE, borderline useless for figuring out where certain rooms are in the house. I struggled to navigate virtually every single time I needed to go somewhere specific. I still have no idea where the billiard room is, despite needing to find that room in particular probably a dozen times. The house is gigantic, and the rooms on the map lack almost all detail; you're lucky if there's a bed to depict one of the million different bedrooms. You also have to stare at the map for a while to even figure out where you currently are, since the only indication is the gentle pulsing of the tiny white lines depicting the room, barely visible.

From an achievement hunting perspective, the achievements are notoriously finicky and unreasonable to unlock. If you look through the community discussions for this game, you will find years and years of people struggling over the exact same issues over and over and over again, with only occasional resolution from a tiny little detail someone shared in desperation YEARS down the line... For my first completion of the game, I got all achievements except the one for reading every note. I spent many hours after that agonizingly reading everything again, over and over, on multiple separate occasions over the years, and never got the achievement. I had to play the entire game all over again to get the achievement, and I still don't even know what note I was missing.

Playing this game filled me with the rage of a thousand suns, and I came back to it after nearly a DECADE in time out, fueled by an intensely bitter vendetta, as well as the desire to finally put it behind me FOREVER! This game will not haunt me anymore!!!!! HAHA!!!!!!!! NOT RECOMMENDED.
